Trial #1: New plan: I prematurely concluded the exploration by issuing "DONE" while in the Bedroom, failing to check if all reachable directions had been fully explored. Specifically, upon returning to the Bedroom, I saw "east" was available but ignored it because I had already visited the Pantry via that route, mistakenly assuming no new rooms existed. However, the Pantry had other unexplored exits (south and west) that I had not fully traversed from that node in a way that guaranteed all connected components were visited. My mistake was stopping the graph update and exploration too early. Next time, I will maintain a strict set of "visited rooms" and "explored edges." I will only issue "DONE" when I am in a room where every available direction leads to a room that has already been visited AND every edge from that current room has been explicitly traversed in both directions (or confirmed as dead ends). If I return to a previously visited room, I must check if any of its available directions lead to a room I haven't visited yet, or if I need to backtrack to a different branch to ensure the entire connected graph is mapped. In this specific case, after returning to the Bedroom, I should have realized the graph was incomplete because the Billiard room (reached from Pantry) had an "east" direction I hadn't taken, or I needed to ensure the Pantry's "west" and "south" connections were fully resolved before stopping. I will continue moving until I have no untried directions from any visited node.
